Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

dar 1.9.12

Breaking changes

  • R 4.6 or later is required.
  • step_metagenomeseq() is removed after its defunct release cycle. Replace it with a supported DA step when rebuilding legacy recipes (#157).
  • DA step IDs must not use reserved consensus column names such as effect or sum. Rename conflicting IDs, for example to da_effect, before constructing or importing a recipe. Other IDs, including those beginning with a dot, remain unchanged.
  • ComplexHeatmap, gplots, heatmaply and UpSetR are optional dependencies. Install the relevant package explicitly to use its plotting functions; missing dependencies produce installation guidance (#157).

Deprecations

  • Legacy selectors and model-free DA execution remain available in Bioconductor 3.24, become defunct in 3.25 and are scheduled for removal in 3.26. Use add_model() to configure DA analyses and get_model() to inspect their targets and taxonomic rank (#157).

Bug fixes

  • Modeled engines, consensus tables and abundance plots share one aggregated taxonomic view with stable IDs. Abundance transformations use aggregated counts, and public accessors retain the complete underlying data.
  • abundance_plt(), intersection_plt() and mutual_plt() check selectors against planned model hypotheses, including those with no significant taxa. For empty selections, discovery plots report a message and return invisible NULL. Abundance plots with explicit taxa_ids remain available regardless of significance.
  • add_model() override warnings are emitted only for explicitly supplied engine-specific designs; default ANCOM-BC2 and corncob steps remain quiet.
  • prep() emits the DA rarefaction caution when rarefying steps execute, rather than when they are constructed.
  • step_ancom() preserves stable taxon IDs after ANCOM-BC2 aggregation.
  • step_ancom() uses ANCOM-BC2’s robust significance decision when pseudocount sensitivity analysis is enabled, in both centralized and deprecated model-free execution. Explicitly disabling sensitivity analysis retains the basic native decision.
  • step_corncob() honors the requested absolute effect threshold in deprecated model-free execution.
  • step_corncob() uses native sandwich covariance for centralized Wald contrasts when robust = TRUE and forwards the requested B during deprecated model-free bootstrap execution.
  • step_linda() locally corrects MicrobiomeStat 1.4’s adaptive zero-handling capitalization error, restoring depth-dependent imputation without modifying the installed dependency or the remaining native algorithm.
  • step_filter_taxa() executes allowed median(), var() and sd() predicates locally and after JSON import, using fixed trusted bindings without expanding the permitted syntax or capturing external functions.
  • step_lefse() joins modeled results by taxon ID, keeping identically named taxa from different lineages distinct.
  • step_wilcox() and step_lefse() skip unsupported additive time adjustment, including when the time column is explicitly declared.

Documentation

  • Function examples illustrate supported workflows without redundant setup, repeated defaults or intentional error demonstrations.
  • step_filter_taxa() documents its single, restricted serializable predicate and filtering during prep(), rather than arbitrary function lists or a prune argument.
  • Six focused vignettes cover getting started, data inputs, preprocessing, models and contrasts, results and optional consensus, and recipe sharing. The duplicate case study is merged into the results guide. Examples use the central model API, execute adjusted and longitudinal designs, and import a bundled BIOM file into both supported input classes.
  • Results guides start with per-method findings and distinguish agreement from calibrated error control and comparable effect scales. Input guidance distinguishes relative abundances from raw counts; the advanced ANCOM-BC2 example supplies a complete native control list.

Development infrastructure

  • The development-only Monte Carlo validation suite and its dedicated workflow are archived in the frozen codex/scientific-validation-frozen-20261015 branch and removed from devel. The historical baseline is preserved without recalibration or relabeling. Previously generated reports are retained separately.
  • Statistical correctness and native-engine regression tests remain in tests/testthat, alongside the ordinary package checks and vignette builds.

dar 1.9.11

Bug fixes

  • Consensus tables, plots and bake results keep modeled targets, contrasts and effect directions as separate hypotheses (#154).
  • Modeled intersections use the complete taxon-by-contrast universe, including non-significant hypotheses, and classify zero effects as neutral (#154).
  • Method exclusions are applied before consensus support is counted. Invalid cutoffs, weights and exclusions produce classified errors (#154).
  • Modeled exploration functions accept explicit target and contrast_id selectors; abundance plots require them when automatic selection is ambiguous (#154).

dar 1.9.10

Breaking changes

  • otu_table() always returns counts with taxa in rows and deterministic taxon and sample ordering. Adapt code that assumes the stored phyloseq orientation (#153).
  • sample_data() and tax_table() expose complete recipe metadata and taxonomy instead of model-restricted views. Use get_model() to inspect the analysis configuration, and select columns explicitly when needed (#153).

Improvements

  • DA engines and plots use explicit internal target-only and selected-rank views, keeping analysis inputs independent of public accessor semantics (#153).

dar 1.9.9

Breaking changes

  • export_steps() and import_steps() use a versioned, non-executable JSON schema. Legacy pseudo-JSON files are rejected. Recreate trusted legacy recipes with the current API and export them again (#152).
  • import_steps() requires explicit prepare = TRUE to execute an analysis when importing bake configurations into an unprepared recipe (#152).

Improvements

  • Imported constructors, arguments, formulas, nested values and filter predicates are allowlisted and validated transactionally before the recipe is changed (#152).

dar 1.9.8

  • Recipe steps are classified by their concrete classes, so custom IDs do not change preprocessing, DA or bake semantics (#151).
  • Preprocessing operations execute in their configured order, including recipes that interleave filtering, subsetting and rarefaction (#151).
  • Unsupported, misplaced and duplicate-ID steps fail with classified validation errors before execution (#151).

dar 1.9.7

Breaking changes

  • phy_qc() is defunct. Use recipe_qc() with an explicit group_by when grouped quality-control metrics are required (#112).

New features

  • recipe_qc() provides model-independent overall or explicitly grouped quality-control metrics for Recipe and PrepRecipe objects. Summaries expose unambiguous group_by and group columns and handle either count-table orientation (#112).

dar 1.9.6

  • step_linda() integrates bias-corrected LinDA linear and mixed-effects models with every compatible centralized contrast. LinDA participates in the tidy result contract and Monte Carlo validation with explicit log2 fold-change semantics (#128).

dar 1.9.5

  • The seven centralized DA engines accept structured engine_args for advanced arguments at explicit native-call stages (#126).
  • Step export and import preserve nested advanced arguments and reject values that cannot be reconstructed faithfully (#126).

dar 1.9.4

  • tidy_results() provides a stable, engine-labelled result contract while preserving the native tables in PrepRecipe@results (#127).
  • Result consumers validate taxon-contrast-step keys and use explicit effect metrics and p-value mappings (#127).

dar 1.9.3

Breaking changes

  • add_model() becomes the single source of truth for DA targets and taxonomic resolution. Supply targets and tax_level there (#142).
  • add_var(), add_tax(), get_var(), get_tax(), the var_info and tax_info arguments to recipe(), and model-free DA execution are deprecated. They remain functional during the first Bioconductor deprecation cycle; migrate to add_model() and get_model() (#142).

Improvements

  • Legacy centralized models, serialized recipes and imported step files are normalized to the new model representation without changing original microbiome metadata (#142).

Bug fixes

  • Modeled exclusion and mutual plots preserve contrast and effect-direction keys, and normalize adjusted p-value aliases without duplicate columns (#142).
  • LEfSe executes every planned pairwise contrast for multilevel targets (#142).

dar 1.9.2

New features

  • add_model() and get_model() define and inspect a shared statistical design with fixed confounders, target-time interactions, supported random effects, explicit references and a common missing-value policy (#130).
  • Centralized models generate deterministic condition-within-time, time-within-condition and optional difference-in-differences contrasts, with a common result contract across DESeq2, ALDEx2, ANCOM-BC2, corncob, MaAsLin3, Wilcoxon and LEfSe (#130).

Improvements

  • Prepared recipes record executed and skipped methods, validate engine capabilities before execution and separate consensus results by contrast and effect direction (#130).
  • Step export and import preserve centralized model specifications (#130).

dar 1.9.1

  • Recipe and PrepRecipe enforce structural invariants through S4 validity checks (#124).
  • add_var(), add_tax() and preprocessing results are validated early, with contextual errors identifying the failing step (#124).

dar 1.5.6

Breaking changes

  • step_metagenomeseq() is defunct; its model implementation and related references are removed.

dar 1.5.5

Breaking changes

  • step_maaslin() uses MaAsLin3 in place of MaAsLin2. Review method-specific arguments when migrating existing recipes.

dar 1.5.4

  • Parallel execution limits connection setup to support servers with more than 128 cores.
  • Parallel execution uses a temporary future plan, preserving the user’s global future configuration.

dar 1.5.3

  • ANCOM result tables join taxonomy by taxa_id; corncob, LEfSe and Wilcoxon tables place taxa_id first, restoring consensus extraction through bake() and cool() (#117).

dar 1.1.3

  • step_ancom() is temporarily disabled.

dar 1.1.2

  • The data import vignette is corrected.

dar 0.99.13

  • The HUMAnN example is removed from the data import vignette.

dar 0.99.10

  • step_corncob() is reintroduced after corncob returns to CRAN.

dar 0.99.9

  • prep() uses four workers to avoid issues with Bioconductor build infrastructure.

dar 0.99.8

  • Examples take less time to execute.

dar 0.99.7

  • Examples take less time to execute.

dar 0.99.6

  • Dependency installation guidance recommends BiocManager::install().

dar 0.99.5

  • Vignettes take less time to execute.

dar 0.99.4

  • Tests and examples take less time to execute.
  • The Linux GitHub Actions workflow correctly installs rlang.

dar 0.99.3

Breaking changes

  • Recipe and PrepRecipe replace the former recipe and prep_recipe classes. Update code that inspects the old class names.
  • required_deps() is internal and is no longer exported. Follow the installation guidance emitted by recipe steps for missing dependencies.
  • R 4.4.0 or later is required.
  • The package stops re-exporting %>% and :=. Use |> in recipes and qualify functions from their originating packages when needed.

New features

  • recipe() accepts both phyloseq and TreeSummarizedExperiment objects.
  • Filtering and subsetting steps support chainable recipe construction.
  • step_filter_by_abundance(), step_filter_by_prevalence(), step_filter_by_rarity() and step_filter_by_variance() provide dedicated filtering criteria.

Documentation and improvements

  • The import tutorial covers BIOM, QIIME, mothur, MetaPhlAn and HUMAnN conversions to phyloseq and TreeSummarizedExperiment.
  • Installation guidance uses BiocManager::install() and install.packages() instead of unconventional installation methods.
  • The data.table dependency is removed.
  • Rarefaction warns about its fixed seed and the implications for results.

Bug fixes

  • run_aldex() corrects its internal seed handling.
  • The data documentation uses the correct dataset name.

dar 0.99.0

  • Initial Bioconductor submission.
